label: starship_class_rtls_starbase: ascent and stage-1 debris recomputed with a native point-mass twin (E8-05), and the given landing corridor re-flown through two independent dynamics models

analytical.label: Analytic solution
analytical.proves: the numerics reproduce the closed-form solution of the model they integrate (the equations and the integrator, not their agreement with reality).
analytical.cannot_prove: that the model represents reality -- the closed-form reference shares the model's own assumptions (point mass, impulsive burns, idealised field).

independent_model.label: Independent model
independent_model.proves: two independently formulated models agree, so neither is trivially mis-implemented.
independent_model.cannot_prove: that either model is right in the real world -- an assumption shared by both stays invisible; the phase and force inventory of the comparison bound its reach.

historical_telemetry.label: Historical telemetry
historical_telemetry.proves: the model reproduces a published, observed (flown) value it was not tuned to.
historical_telemetry.cannot_prove: any other vehicle, phase or operating point -- one published event validates that event, not the model as a whole, and the reference's own provenance is only as good as its source.

design_input.label: Matches design input
design_input.proves: the solver reached the aim point, or the plan respects the site/vehicle/corridor envelope it was designed against -- internal consistency only.
design_input.cannot_prove: anything about fidelity to reality: the reference IS the design input, so this is NOT independent validation and must never be read as historical proof.

numerical_consistency.label: Numerical consistency
numerical_consistency.proves: integration error is under tolerance and the model's own invariants / self-consistency hold (step convergence, exact integrals, a same-model re-fly).
numerical_consistency.cannot_prove: agreement with any other model or with reality -- it bounds numerical error only.

reference.description: E5-08 new-vehicle qualification mission (Starship-class RTLS-derived design: the E5-07 reference stack with the DC1 powered-entry RTLS scheme; ascent recorded computed, booster recovery FLOWN through the shipped E3 chain, full_mission declared -- the closure E5-07 reported as a gap)

ascent.meco.state_position.basis: point-mass twin vs the recorded OT state history at MECO; measured ~2.2e2 m nominal, almost all of it the engine-Isp line; band = measured + ~80% margin for probe-interaction terms charged to it

ascent.meco.state_velocity.basis: measured ~15 m/s nominal, engine-Isp line; margin on MECO mass-deficit line (Isp law mismatch ~1.2% of stage-1 burn)

ascent.meco.mass.basis: stage-1 burnout mass deficit is the engine-Isp line: pad 329.26 s vs authored 327 s (linear laws), ~1.2% of the 1.2 Mt stage-1 propellant

ascent.separation.state_position.basis: coasted 3 s from MECO; measured ~2.4e2 m; band covers the carried MECO offset plus coast propagation of the same discrepancy

ascent.separation.state_velocity.basis: the MECO velocity offset, coasted 3 s nearly unchanged; measured ~5.4 m/s with the same engine-line origin

ascent.separation.debris_mass.basis: debris mass = twin separation mass - 1.3 Mt ship vs recorded body mass; engine line again; measured ~6.4e3 kg

ascent.seco.state_position.basis: 378 s of stage-2 burn accumulate the (smaller, +0.3 s equivalent) Isp-law offset plus gravity-loss-path drift; measured ~2.7e3 m

ascent.seco.state_velocity.basis: measured ~7 m/s; margin for the stage-2 mass-flow-line offset

ascent.seco.mass.basis: measured ~5e1 kg: the stage-2 Isp line is declared from the recorded vacuum Isp directly, so only integration-path terms remain

ascent.meco.residual_position.basis: nominal MECO position discrepancy minus the measured engine/aero/numerical budget lines; what remains is interaction terms, engine-model shape differences and throttle-schedule tracking

ascent.meco.residual_velocity.basis: residual MECO velocity discrepancy after the three measured lines: the part of the engine-model difference invisible from the raw state history (ambient thrust correction and mass-flow shape) coupled through the gravity-turn path; measured 13.2 m/s

ascent.separation.residual_position.basis: residual at separation: carries the MECO residual forward through 3 s of coast, plus coast-integration cross terms

ascent.seco.residual_position.basis: residual at SECO after 378 s of stage-2 burn: accumulated path difference not explained by the three measured probe lines

ascent.maxq.value.basis: max-q agreement of two point-mass models sharing the CA polar: measured ~3e1 Pa (-0.08%); band ~3%

ascent.maxq.time.basis: max-q is a broad maximum; phase offset follows the thrust-rise line; measured -0.9 s

ascent.seco.orbit_semi_major_axis.basis: osculating elements from both SECO states with the same closed form; the semi-major axis follows the velocity discrepancy, da ~ 2*a*dv/v (about 1.75 km per m/s here), so the band is the SECO velocity band seen through vis-viva; measured 8.5 km

ascent.seco.orbit_eccentricity.basis: tracks the SECO state band; measured ~1e-4

ascent.seco.orbit_inclination.basis: the attitude program fixes the azimuth profile; inclination discrepancy is second-order in the state offset

ascent.debris_impact.time.basis: emergent check: debris ballistic range is sensitive to the (engine-line-shifted) separation state and to CA power-off +/-30% (vehicle file); measured +2 s

ascent.debris_impact.speed.basis: impact speed vs recorded (both Earth-relative); measured ~8.5%; the power-off CA table is an illustrative blunt-body polar

landing.cutoff_position.basis: re-flight disagreement at the commanded cutoff node: the two re-integrators fly the same profile through different gravity/atmosphere/replay implementations; measured ~6 m vertical

landing.cutoff_velocity.basis: same comparison at the cutoff node; measured ~0.9 m/s

landing.touchdown_position.basis: touchdown position disagreement between the two re-flights; measured ~0.3 m (both converge toward the pad target)

landing.touchdown_vertical_speed.basis: touchdown vertical-speed disagreement: amplifies the cutoff-state offset ballistically (the cutoff is a fixed-clock engine stop, so a cutoff-height error dh enters as sqrt(v^2+2g dh)); the *design limit* 3 m/s is graded on the FL-301 re-flight alone (design_input)

landing.touchdown_lateral_speed.basis: measured ~0.25 m/s: the crossrange channels barely diverge between the two re-flights; band leaves 10x margin on the observed disagreement

landing.propellant.basis: propellant-burned disagreement at touchdown between the re-flights (same Isp law, different replay/integration); measured ~1.6e2 kg

probes.engine: twin re-run with the recorded pad Isp 329.26 s (the difference between the authored YAML Isp law and the recorded OpenTsiolkovsky Isp law)
probes.aero: twin re-run with atmosphere density x1.03 (US76 vs the recorded program's own atmosphere model, ~3% band near sea level)

assumption_differences: ascent: the two models share the authored attitude program, throttle schedules and vehicle constants (design inputs); they differ in formulation (external OpenTsiolkovsky vs the repo 3-DOF plant), in the engine Isp law (YAML linear-in-pressure law, pad 327 s, vs the recorded pad 329.26 s law -- the measured engine line), the atmosphere (US76 x1.03 band -- the measured aero line) and the integrator step (RK4 0.02 s vs the recorded program's own scheme -- the measured numerical line).

ascent frame: both sides expressed in the launch-aligned ECI-at-t=0 convention (raw columns rotated by R3(-omega*t)); the t=0 pad state agrees to < 1 m, which is why the frame/time line is declared zero rather than fitted.

debris: the twin's re-entry is a separately written variable-mass-free ballistic integrator with the power-off CA polar from the same YAML; OpenTsiolkovsky integrates its own debris body; the impact comparison is therefore an emergent, widest-band check.

landing: the corridor insertion state is the cool DECLARED design input (the E5-07 convention), flown on this derived vehicle's own 3-engine landing set; both re-flights share the gfold plan nodes and the landing configuration declared from the vehicle file's own note; they differ in gravity (J2 point-mass + centrifugal vs IGF-80 normal gravity with the centrifugal absorbed, Coriolis omitted -- below 0.15 m on this arc), atmosphere (FL-301's entry density table vs independent US76 tables), command replay (node-acceleration FOH x current mass vs physical-thrust FOH with the engine's own ambient correction and throttle limits) and integrator (RK4 0.1 s vs RK4 0.05 s).
no check in this report uses historical_telemetry evidence: the reference vehicle is a public estimate, not flown hardware, and there is no telemetry to compare against.
honesty_notes: E8-01's comparisons of the chain against OpenTsiolkovsky's own raw output are extraction/serialisation checks and are relabelled numerical_consistency/analytical in full_chain; the independent ascent-model evidence for the E5-07 reference is this module's twin, and only this module's.
Residual lines are reported, never zeroed; where a probe over-explains (negative line), the surplus is carried in the residual.

actual_recorded_corridor.note: the actual corridor insertion state this mission reached, probed with the same two-model E8-05 machinery on the declared 3-engine landing set. It is UNPLANNABLE from here -- the independent models agree with the E3 planner that no soft landing exists inside the reserve at this arrival state, corroborating the landing gap (RECOVERY_GAP_E508.md). The powered-landing SYSTEM is validated above on the cool declared design corridor in the 3-engine configuration, exactly as in the E5-07 reference.
